findings.title: AWS Data Exchange
findings.summary: Both - free and paid datasets available — Global - available in multiple AWS regions worldwide
findings.details: Scale: Approximately 3,500+ data products from 300+ data providers (as of early 2025, estimated). One of the largest cloud-native data marketplaces.

findings.title: Snowflake Marketplace
findings.summary: Both - many free datasets available alongside paid/commercial listings — Global - available across all Snowflake cloud regions (AWS, Azure, GCP)
findings.details: Scale: Approximately 2,000+ listings from 500+ data providers (as of early 2025, estimated). Rapidly growing. Snowflake reports thousands of data shares happening daily across its platform.

findings.title: Databricks Marketplace
findings.summary: Both - includes free open datasets and paid commercial data products — Global - available across Databricks deployments on AWS, Azure, and GCP
findings.details: Scale: Approximately 1,500+ listings (as of early 2025, estimated). Growing rapidly since GA launch. Includes data products from major providers like Nasdaq, Foursquare, and others.

findings.title: Azure Data Marketplace (Microsoft Azure Marketplace - Data category) / Azure Open Datasets
findings.summary: Both - Azure Open Datasets are free; Azure Marketplace data products include both free and paid offerings — Global, with a strong emphasis on US government and public datasets. Azure Open Datasets includes international data from multiple countries.
findings.details: Scale: Azure Open Datasets: approximately 100+ curated public datasets. Azure Marketplace (data category): hundreds of data product listings from numerous providers. The broader Azure Marketplace contains tens of thousands of total listings across all categories.

findings.title: Google Cloud Analytics Hub
findings.summary: Both - many free public datasets via Google BigQuery Public Datasets; Analytics Hub supports both free and commercial data exchanges — Global - available in all Google Cloud regions. BigQuery Public Datasets lean toward US-centric sources but include significant international data.
findings.details: Scale: BigQuery Public Datasets: 200+ datasets. Analytics Hub: growing number of commercial and internal listings (exact count not widely published). Google Dataset Search indexes millions of datasets across the web (but is a search engine, not a marketplace).

findings.title: Oracle Data Marketplace
findings.summary: Both - includes free and paid data product listings — Global - available across Oracle Cloud regions. Strong presence in enterprise markets in North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
findings.details: Scale: The Oracle Cloud Marketplace overall has thousands of listings, but the data-specific category is smaller compared to AWS or Snowflake - estimated hundreds of data-related listings. Oracle's data marketplace is less prominent as a standalone offering compared to competitors.

findings.title: SAP Data Marketplace
findings.summary: Both - includes free sample/open data and commercial paid data products — Global - with a strong presence in Europe (SAP's home market) and enterprise markets worldwide
findings.details: Scale: Estimated hundreds of data product listings. Growing since SAP Datasphere rebrand and investment. Smaller than AWS or Snowflake marketplaces but highly focused on enterprise and business data.

findings.title: IBM Data Exchange / IBM Data Asset eXchange (DAX) / IBM Environmental Intelligence Suite Data
findings.summary: Primarily free and open-source (IBM Data Asset eXchange). IBM's commercial data offerings are available through IBM Cloud and IBM Environmental Intelligence Suite. — Global - open datasets are accessible worldwide. Commercial offerings available in IBM Cloud regions.
findings.details: Scale: IBM Data Asset eXchange: approximately 30-50 curated open datasets (smaller, highly curated collection). IBM's commercial data offerings (Weather Company, etc.) serve thousands of enterprise customers. The scale is more about data quality and curation than breadth of listings.

findings.title: Ocean Protocol
findings.summary: Both - free to list, transaction fees apply; OCEAN token used for staking and transactions — Global
findings.details: Scale: Thousands of datasets listed on Ocean Market. OCEAN token has been a top-200 cryptocurrency by market cap. Active developer community. Total Value Locked has fluctuated with crypto markets.

findings.title: Streamr
findings.summary: Both - free tier available, paid for premium streams and higher throughput — Global
findings.details: Scale: Thousands of active streams. Network of broker nodes globally distributed. Community of developers building on the protocol. DATA token is a smaller-cap cryptocurrency.

findings.title: Harbr (Harbr Data Commerce)
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise B2B platform — Global, primarily UK and US enterprise market
findings.details: Scale: Enterprise clients include financial data firms and media companies. Relatively niche B2B platform. Not a public marketplace - provides infrastructure for clients to build their own.

findings.title: CARTO Data Observatory
findings.summary: Both - some free/open datasets accessible; premium datasets require CARTO subscription or additional licensing — Global coverage, strong in US and Europe
findings.details: Scale: Thousands of curated spatial datasets from dozens of providers. Covers 190+ countries for some dataset categories.

findings.title: Knoema
findings.summary: Both - free access to public/open statistical data; premium plans for advanced features and proprietary datasets — Global - aggregates data from 200+ countries. Sources include World Bank, IMF, UN, national statistical offices, and proprietary sources.
findings.details: Scale: Claims billions of data points from thousands of sources covering virtually every country. One of the largest aggregators of public statistical data.

findings.title: Statista
findings.summary: Both - limited free access to some statistics; full access requires paid subscription — Global coverage with particularly strong data for US, Europe, and major economies. Offices in Hamburg, New York, London, and other cities.
findings.details: Scale: 1,000,000+ statistics across 80,000+ topics from 22,500+ sources. Major global platform for business statistics. Over 1 billion annual page views claimed.

findings.title: data.ai (formerly App Annie)
findings.summary: Both - limited free tier (app rankings, basic estimates); paid subscriptions for detailed analytics — Global - covers iOS App Store and Google Play across all countries
findings.details: Scale: Tracks millions of apps across iOS and Google Play. Estimates for 150+ countries. Previously the largest independent mobile analytics provider.

findings.title: Similarweb
findings.summary: Both - free browser extension and limited web lookups; paid platform subscriptions — Global - estimates for websites and apps worldwide
findings.details: Scale: Estimates traffic for 100M+ websites. Data from panel of hundreds of millions of devices, ISP partnerships, and direct measurement. Major global digital intelligence provider.

findings.title: BattleFin
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/institutional — Primarily US and Europe (financial centers)
findings.details: Scale: Catalogs hundreds of alternative data providers. Events attract major hedge funds and asset managers. Niche but influential in alternative data ecosystem.

findings.title: Eagle Alpha
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/institutional — Global, primarily serving US and European financial institutions
findings.details: Scale: Catalogs and evaluates hundreds of alternative data providers. Serves institutional investors globally. Published influential annual alternative data surveys.

findings.title: Common Crawl
findings.summary: Free - entirely open and free to use — Global web - crawls billions of pages across all languages and countries
findings.details: Scale: Each monthly crawl contains 3-5+ billion web pages. Total archive spans 10+ years of monthly crawls. Hundreds of petabytes of total data. Used to train many of the world's largest language models.

findings.title: Zenodo
findings.summary: Free - open access research data repository — Global academic/research community
findings.details: Scale: Millions of records. One of the largest general-purpose open research data repositories. Growing rapidly as open science mandates increase.

findings.title: Dryad
findings.summary: Free to access. Publishing fees for depositors (often covered by institutions or journal agreements). — Global academic community, strong in US and Europe
findings.details: Scale: Tens of thousands of curated datasets. Primarily focused on data associated with peer-reviewed publications.

findings.title: Figshare
findings.summary: Both - free personal accounts with storage limits; institutional and publisher versions are paid — Global academic community
findings.details: Scale: Millions of research outputs hosted. Used by hundreds of institutions worldwide. One of the most popular research data repositories.

findings.title: ICPSR (Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research)
findings.summary: Both - some data freely available; full access requires institutional membership — Primarily US data, but includes international datasets. US institutional membership base.
findings.details: Scale: Over 16,000 studies with over 250,000 files. 800+ member institutions. One of the world's largest archives of social science data.

findings.title: Harvard Dataverse
findings.summary: Free - open access repository — Global. Harvard Dataverse is the largest installation, but Dataverse software is used by dozens of institutions worldwide.
findings.details: Scale: Harvard Dataverse alone hosts 100,000+ datasets. Dozens of other institutions run their own Dataverse installations. One of the most widely-used research data repository platforms.

findings.title: Definitive Healthcare
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise subscription with limited free lookups — Primarily United States
findings.details: Scale: Covers virtually all US hospitals, physician groups, and healthcare facilities. Millions of provider records. Billions of claims records analyzed.

findings.title: IQVIA (formerly IMS Health / Quintiles IMS)
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/institutional — Global - operates in 100+ countries. Particularly strong in US, Europe, Japan.
findings.details: Scale: Analyzes data from 150,000+ data suppliers. Patient-level data on over 1 billion de-identified patient records. $15B+ annual revenue (data, technology, and services combined). 86,000+ employees.

findings.title: Zillow Data Products (ZTRAX / Zillow Research)
findings.summary: Both - Zillow Research data is free; ZTRAX (transaction/assessment data) was free for researchers but access has been restricted — United States (comprehensive coverage)
findings.details: Scale: Covers 100M+ US properties. ZTRAX contains hundreds of millions of transaction records. Research data covers all US metros/states.

findings.title: Reonomy
findings.summary: Paid - subscription-based platform — United States - comprehensive national CRE coverage
findings.details: Scale: Covers 50M+ commercial and residential properties in the US. Millions of commercial property records with ownership data.

findings.title: ATTOM Data Solutions
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise data licensing — United States - nationwide property data coverage
findings.details: Scale: 155M+ US residential and commercial properties. 99%+ county coverage. Billions of data points across property, transaction, and risk categories.

findings.title: Tomorrow.io (formerly ClimaCell)
findings.summary: Both - free tier for basic weather API; paid plans for advanced features and data — Global coverage with minute-by-minute resolution
findings.details: Scale: Global coverage. Hundreds of millions of API calls served. Backed by over $400M in venture funding. Building satellite constellation for proprietary data.

findings.title: DTN (formerly Data Transmission Network)
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/commercial subscriptions — Global, with particularly strong presence in North America
findings.details: Scale: Serves thousands of enterprise clients across agriculture, energy, and transportation. Decades of historical weather and market data.

findings.title: Replica
findings.summary: Paid - government/enterprise subscriptions — United States - growing metro area coverage
findings.details: Scale: Covers most major US metro areas. Used by dozens of state DOTs and metropolitan planning organizations.

findings.title: StreetLight Data
findings.summary: Paid - subscription/project-based — United States and Canada primarily
findings.details: Scale: Processes trillions of location data points. Covers all US roads. Used by hundreds of government agencies and planning firms.

findings.title: Lightcast (formerly Emsi Burning Glass)
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise subscriptions. Some free tools (e.g., Open Skills Library). — Primarily US, UK, Canada, Australia. Expanding to more countries.
findings.details: Scale: Processes billions of job postings historically. Covers millions of employer profiles. Used by thousands of educational institutions and employers.

findings.title: Revelio Labs
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise subscriptions — Primarily US, growing international coverage
findings.details: Scale: Tracks hundreds of millions of professional profiles. Coverage of most large public and private companies in the US.

findings.title: Hugging Face Datasets
findings.summary: Both - mostly free community datasets; Hugging Face Pro/Enterprise subscriptions for additional features — Global
findings.details: Scale: 100,000+ public datasets. Millions of monthly users. The de facto standard hub for ML datasets. Hosts some of the most important AI training datasets.

findings.title: Papers with Code Datasets
findings.summary: Free - open index of ML datasets linked to academic papers — Global academic and research community
findings.details: Scale: Indexes thousands of datasets with links to papers and benchmarks. Comprehensive coverage of ML research datasets.

findings.title: Roboflow
findings.summary: Both - free tier for public projects; paid plans for private projects and advanced features — Global
findings.details: Scale: Roboflow Universe hosts 200,000+ public computer vision datasets. Platform used by tens of thousands of developers. Rapidly growing.

findings.title: Scale AI (Scale Data Engine / Scale Catalog)
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/project-based — Global - headquartered in US with labeling workforce worldwide
findings.details: Scale: One of the highest-valued AI infrastructure companies (~$14B valuation). Hundreds of millions in revenue. Labeled data for most major autonomous vehicle and AI companies.

findings.title: Ocean Protocol Predictoor
findings.summary: Paid - uses OCEAN tokens for predictions — Global (blockchain-based)
findings.details: Scale: Newer product, still building adoption. Part of the broader Ocean Protocol ecosystem.

findings.title: Filecoin / Filecoin Data Economy
findings.summary: Both - storage costs paid in FIL token; data retrieval may be free or paid depending on provider — Global decentralized network
findings.details: Scale: Exabytes of storage capacity on the network. Thousands of storage providers globally. FIL is a top-50 cryptocurrency by market cap.

findings.title: The Graph
findings.summary: Both - free hosted service (being deprecated) and paid decentralized network queries — Global (blockchain-based)
findings.details: Scale: Billions of queries served. Thousands of active subgraphs. Core infrastructure for DeFi and Web3 data access.

findings.title: Chainlink (Data Feeds / CCIP)
findings.summary: Both - reading price feeds is free for consumers; node operators are paid by protocols — Global (blockchain-based)
findings.details: Scale: Secures tens of billions of dollars in DeFi value. Hundreds of price feeds across multiple blockchains. LINK is a top-20 cryptocurrency. Used by most major DeFi protocols.

findings.title: Dawex
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise data exchange platform — Europe-focused, particularly France. Aligned with EU data sovereignty initiatives (Gaia-X).
findings.details: Scale: Powers several European data exchange initiatives. Focused on B2B enterprise market rather than consumer-scale.

findings.title: Datarade
findings.summary: Free to search/browse; data purchases are between buyers and providers — Global
findings.details: Scale: 2,000+ listed data providers. Thousands of data products cataloged. Growing as a data commerce intermediary.

findings.title: Narrative
findings.summary: Both - free to list/browse; transaction fees on data purchases — Primarily US, expanding globally
findings.details: Scale: Billions of data points available. Growing provider network. Focused on programmatic data commerce.

findings.title: Databricks Marketplace
findings.summary: Both - free and paid datasets available; requires Databricks account — Global
findings.details: Scale: Growing marketplace. Hundreds of data providers. Leverages Databricks' large enterprise customer base.

findings.title: Kaggle Datasets
findings.summary: Free — Global
findings.details: Scale: 200,000+ public datasets. 15M+ registered users. One of the largest data science communities globally.

findings.title: Labelbox
findings.summary: Both - free tier available; paid plans for larger projects — Global
findings.details: Scale: Used by enterprises and AI teams globally. Competitor to Scale AI in the labeling space.

findings.title: Appen (formerly Figure Eight / CrowdFlower)
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/project-based — Global - crowd workforce in 170+ countries. Multilingual capabilities.
findings.details: Scale: Global crowd of 1M+ annotators. Major clients include FAANG companies. Revenue of several hundred million USD (though declining).

findings.title: Snowflake Marketplace
findings.summary: Both - free and paid listings available; requires Snowflake account — Global
findings.details: Scale: 2,000+ listings. 500+ providers. Rapidly growing as Snowflake's customer base expands (9,000+ customers). Major cloud data marketplace.

findings.title: LAION (Large-scale Artificial Intelligence Open Network)
findings.summary: Free - open-source datasets — Global (web-sourced data)
findings.details: Scale: LAION-5B: 5.85 billion image-text pairs. One of the largest open datasets ever created for AI training.

findings.title: Dune Analytics
findings.summary: Both - free tier with public queries; paid plans for private queries and more features — Global (blockchain data)
findings.details: Scale: Indexes major blockchains completely. Hundreds of thousands of community-created queries and dashboards. Major platform for crypto analytics.

findings.title: Nansen
findings.summary: Paid - subscription plans with limited free features — Global (blockchain data)
findings.details: Scale: Labels millions of blockchain wallets. Covers major blockchains. Growing user base among crypto traders and funds.

findings.title: Crunchbase
findings.summary: Both - limited free access; paid subscriptions for full data — Global, strongest coverage for US tech/startup ecosystem
findings.details: Scale: Profiles on 1M+ companies, 500K+ people, 200K+ investors. Comprehensive funding data going back decades.

findings.title: PitchBook
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise subscription — Global, comprehensive coverage of US, Europe, Asia-Pacific private markets
findings.details: Scale: Covers 3M+ companies, 1.5M+ deals, 300K+ investors. Gold standard for private market data. Morningstar subsidiary.

findings.title: SafeGraph (now Dewey)
findings.summary: Both - Dewey offers free academic access to some datasets; commercial licensing for business use — United States primarily, some global coverage
findings.details: Scale: Millions of POI records in the US. Significant academic user base inherited from SafeGraph.

findings.title: Bright Data (formerly Luminati Networks)
findings.summary: Paid - usage-based pricing — Global web data collection
findings.details: Scale: 72M+ residential IP addresses in proxy network. Serves thousands of enterprise clients. One of the largest web data collection companies globally.

findings.title: Flatfile
findings.summary: Both - free tier; paid plans for higher volume — Global
findings.details: Scale: Used by thousands of SaaS companies for data onboarding.

findings.title: LiveRamp Data Marketplace
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/advertising industry — Primarily US, expanding internationally
findings.details: Scale: Connects thousands of data providers with advertisers. Identity graph covers most US adults. $500M+ annual revenue.

findings.title: Explorium
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise platform — Global data sourced; primarily US and European clients
findings.details: Scale: Aggregates data from thousands of external sources. Growing enterprise client base in financial services.

findings.title: Thinknum Alternative Data
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/institutional — Primarily US companies tracked, with growing international coverage
findings.details: Scale: Tracks 500K+ companies across dozens of web-scraped data types. Used by hundreds of investment firms.

findings.title: Quandl (now part of Nasdaq)
findings.summary: Both - some free datasets; premium data requires subscription — Global financial data
findings.details: Scale: Hundreds of data products from dozens of providers. Millions of time series. Core infrastructure for quantitative finance data access.

findings.title: Gravy Analytics (formerly UberMedia)
findings.summary: Paid - enterprise/data licensing — Primarily United States
findings.details: Scale: Processes billions of location signals. Covers US retail and commercial locations.

findings.title: Veraset
findings.summary: Both - free for academic/non-profit research; paid commercial licensing — United States, with international expansion
findings.details: Scale: Tracks tens of millions of devices in the US. Daily-updating panel data.

findings.title: Hugging Face (Platform - broader than just Datasets)
findings.summary: Both - free for public usage; Pro and Enterprise tiers for advanced features — Global
findings.details: Scale: 500,000+ public models. 100,000+ datasets. Millions of users. Dominant ML platform.

findings.title: OpenAlex
findings.summary: Free - completely open — Global academic literature
findings.details: Scale: 250M+ works, 100M+ authors, 100K+ institutions. Comprehensive coverage of global scholarly literature.

findings.title: Databento
findings.summary: Paid - usage-based — US markets primarily (CME, Nasdaq, NYSE, CBOE, etc.). Expanding.
findings.details: Scale: Covers major US exchanges. Growing data coverage and exchange partnerships.

findings.title: Polygon.io
findings.summary: Both - free basic tier; paid plans for real-time and higher-volume access — Primarily US financial markets
findings.details: Scale: Covers all US stocks, options, forex, and crypto. Serves thousands of developers and FinTech applications.

findings.title: Data.gov (US Federal Open Data)
findings.summary: Free — United States (federal, state, and local government data)
findings.details: Scale: ~250,000+ datasets harvested from federal agencies (as of 2024-2025). Note: the actual count fluctuates as agencies add/remove datasets.

findings.title: Data.gov.uk (UK Open Data Portal)
findings.summary: Free — United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland)
findings.details: Scale: ~55,000-60,000 datasets from ~1,000+ publishers (as of 2024-2025)

findings.title: Official Portal for European Data (data.europa.eu)
findings.summary: Free — European Union member states and associated countries (pan-European)
findings.details: Scale: ~1,600,000+ datasets harvested from 36+ countries and EU institutions (as of 2024-2025). This is a meta-portal aggregating from national portals.

findings.title: Kaggle Datasets
findings.summary: Free (with optional paid compute tiers) — Global (community-contributed datasets from worldwide sources)
findings.details: Scale: ~300,000+ public datasets (as of 2024-2025, growing rapidly from community contributions)

findings.title: World Bank Open Data
findings.summary: Free — Global (217 economies/countries, with special focus on developing nations)
findings.details: Scale: ~20,000+ indicators across 217 economies. The Microdata Library contains 5,000+ surveys. Multiple databases including WDI, International Debt Statistics, Doing Business (archived), etc.

findings.title: UNdata
findings.summary: Free — Global (all UN member states, ~193 countries)
findings.details: Scale: ~60+ databases from 30+ UN system organizations, containing millions of data records across hundreds of indicators

findings.title: OECD Data
findings.summary: Free (mostly) — OECD member countries (38 members as of 2025) plus key partner economies. Primarily developed/advanced economies.
findings.details: Scale: ~800+ datasets covering thousands of indicators across 38+ countries. Billions of data points in the full OECD.Stat system.

findings.title: WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO)
findings.summary: Free — Global (194 WHO member states)
findings.details: Scale: ~2,300+ indicators across 194 countries with time series data. Covers key global health topics comprehensively.

findings.title: NASA Open Data Portal
findings.summary: Free — Global/Universal (Earth observation is global; space data covers the solar system and beyond)
findings.details: Scale: data.nasa.gov catalog lists ~40,000+ datasets. NASA Earthdata system holds petabytes of Earth science data. The full NASA data ecosystem is massive across multiple specialized archives.

findings.title: NOAA Climate Data (National Centers for Environmental Information)
findings.summary: Free — Global (with especially dense coverage in the United States)
findings.details: Scale: Tens of petabytes of environmental data. NCEI is the world's largest active archive of weather and climate data. Billions of weather observations from stations worldwide.

findings.title: U.S. Census Bureau Data
findings.summary: Free — United States (national, state, county, city, census tract, block group, ZIP code levels)
findings.details: Scale: Hundreds of datasets covering the entire U.S. population. The Census API provides access to billions of data points across multiple surveys and geographies.

findings.title: data.world
findings.summary: Both (freemium model) — Global (community-contributed datasets from worldwide sources)
findings.details: Scale: ~100,000+ public datasets from community contributors and organizations (as of 2024-2025)

findings.title: OpenDataSoft
findings.summary: Both (freemium for portals; data access is free) — Global (especially strong in Europe, particularly France). Powers portals for cities and organizations worldwide.
findings.details: Scale: Powers 300+ open data portals worldwide. The Data Hub indexes 30,000+ datasets from these portals.

findings.title: Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX)
findings.summary: Free — Global, with emphasis on countries affected by humanitarian crises (Sub-Saharan Africa, Middle East, South/Southeast Asia, etc.)
findings.details: Scale: ~20,000+ datasets from 1,500+ organizations covering 250+ locations (as of 2024-2025)

findings.title: Registry of Open Data on AWS
findings.summary: Free (data access); compute costs may apply — Global
findings.details: Scale: ~500+ curated datasets, many of which are massive (petabyte-scale). Includes landmark datasets like Landsat, Sentinel-2, NEXRAD, 1000 Genomes Project, etc.

findings.title: Google Dataset Search
findings.summary: Free (search engine; data availability depends on source) — Global (indexes datasets from all countries and organizations)
findings.details: Scale: Indexes ~25+ million datasets across the web (as of 2023-2024 estimates). Continuously growing as more sites adopt Schema.org markup.

findings.title: Datahub.io
findings.summary: Free (core datasets) — Global
findings.details: Scale: ~1,000+ core/curated datasets. The platform focuses on quality over quantity.

findings.title: Open Data Network (Tyler Data & Insights, formerly Socrata)
findings.summary: Free (data access); platform is commercial SaaS — Primarily United States (federal, state, and local government). Some international government portals also use the platform.
findings.details: Scale: The Open Data Network indexes ~170,000+ datasets across thousands of Socrata/Tyler-powered portals. Individual portals range from hundreds to tens of thousands of datasets.

findings.title: Canada Open Government Portal
findings.summary: Free — Canada (federal government data; some provincial data)
findings.details: Scale: ~90,000+ datasets from federal departments and agencies (as of 2024-2025)

findings.title: data.gov.au (Australian Government Open Data Portal)
findings.summary: Free — Australia (federal, state/territory, and local government data)
findings.details: Scale: ~95,000+ datasets from federal, state, and local government sources (as of 2024-2025)

findings.title: data.gov.in (India Open Government Data Platform)
findings.summary: Free — India (national, state, and district level data)
findings.details: Scale: ~500,000+ resources/catalogs from 150+ government departments (as of 2024-2025). India's portal is one of the largest by catalog count globally, though many entries are individual tables/views rather than distinct datasets.

findings.title: NASA Earthdata
findings.summary: Free — Global (Earth observation data covering the entire planet)
findings.details: Scale: Over 60 petabytes of Earth science data across 12 DAACs, growing by several petabytes per year. Thousands of data products from hundreds of satellite missions.

findings.title: Eurostat
findings.summary: Free — European Union member states, EFTA countries, candidate countries, and some partner countries
findings.details: Scale: ~7,500+ datasets covering thousands of indicators. Billions of data points with extensive time series (some going back to the 1950s).

findings.title: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)
findings.summary: Free — Primarily United States, with some international economic data
findings.details: Scale: ~800,000+ time series from 100+ sources. One of the most comprehensive free economic data platforms in the world.

findings.title: IMF Data
findings.summary: Free — Global (190 member countries)
findings.details: Scale: Multiple major databases covering 190 countries with extensive time series. International Financial Statistics alone covers 32,000+ time series.

findings.title: FAO Data (FAOSTAT)
findings.summary: Free — Global (245+ countries and territories)
findings.details: Scale: Over 20,000 indicators across 245+ countries/territories. Time series data from 1961 to present for many indicators.

findings.title: Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF)
findings.summary: Free — Global (data from every continent including Antarctica)
findings.details: Scale: ~2.6+ billion occurrence records from 85,000+ datasets published by 1,800+ institutions (as of 2024-2025). One of the largest biodiversity databases in the world.

findings.title: arXiv Dataset / Papers with Code
findings.summary: Free — Global
findings.details: Scale: ~8,000+ datasets cataloged with benchmark results and paper linkages (as of 2024-2025)

findings.title: Zenodo
findings.summary: Free — Global (international research community)
findings.details: Scale: ~3+ million records (publications, datasets, software combined). Rapidly growing as open science mandates increase.

findings.title: UCI Machine Learning Repository
findings.summary: Free — Global (academic dataset repository)
findings.details: Scale: ~660+ datasets (as of 2024-2025). Focused on quality and citation impact rather than quantity.

findings.title: OpenStreetMap (OSM)
findings.summary: Free — Global (worldwide coverage, quality varies by region)
findings.details: Scale: ~10+ billion nodes, 1+ billion ways, 15+ million relations. Over 9 million registered contributors. One of the largest collaborative geospatial databases in the world.

findings.title: Data.CDC.gov (CDC Open Data)
findings.summary: Free — United States (national, state, county, and sometimes sub-county levels)
findings.details: Scale: ~1,000+ datasets on the Socrata portal. Additional data available through CDC WONDER and other CDC data systems.

findings.title: New York City Open Data
findings.summary: Free — New York City (five boroughs)
findings.details: Scale: ~3,000+ datasets from 100+ city agencies

findings.title: Copernicus Open Access Hub / Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem
findings.summary: Free — Global (Sentinel satellites provide worldwide coverage)
findings.details: Scale: Petabytes of satellite data. Sentinel missions produce ~12+ terabytes of data per day. Full archive available.

findings.title: GenBank / NCBI Databases
findings.summary: Free — Global (international sequence database consortium member)
findings.details: Scale: GenBank contains ~250+ million sequences. SRA contains petabytes of sequencing data. PubMed indexes 36+ million citations. PubChem has 110+ million compounds. Collectively the largest biomedical data resource in the world.

findings.title: Japan e-Stat
findings.summary: Free — Japan (national, prefectural, and municipal levels)
findings.details: Scale: ~750+ statistical datasets covering virtually all aspects of Japanese society and economy

findings.title: Brazil dados.gov.br
findings.summary: Free — Brazil (federal, state, and municipal data)
findings.details: Scale: ~10,000+ datasets from federal agencies and some state/municipal sources

findings.title: Mexico datos.gob.mx
